Outer Spaces

In 2027, _Outer Spaces_ brings together exhibitions that explore space, time and perception. Artistic perspectives examine the relationship between humanity and the universe, challenge familiar notions and open up new ways of seeing the world and beyond.

# Neue Galerie Graz

## BRUSEUM

Today: 10:00 - 18:00

Fine art from the 19th century to the present.

[Exhibitions](https://www.museum-joanneum.at/en/neue-galerie-graz/our-programme/exhibitions) [BRUSEUM](https://www.museum-joanneum.at/en/neue-galerie-graz/discover/collection/bruseum)

Today

Neue Galerie Graz As one of the largest and most important in the country, the collection of the Neue Galerie Graz with the BRUSEUM comprises more than 70,000 works by Austrian and international artists from the 19th century to the present, from a wide variety of media, from regionally to internationally important positions.

1895

The museum building in Neutorgasse is erected. It houses the two collections on which the Neue Galerie Graz collection is based - the painting gallery of the Estates Drawing Academy and the art collection of the Joanneum. 

1941

Separation of the Landesbildergalerie into the Alte Galerie and the Neue Galerie and transfer of the collection to the Palais Herberstein in Sackstraße. While the collection of the Alte Galerie included art up to 1800, the Neue Galerie took over the holdings of the 19th and 20th centuries.

2011

In the course of the reconstruction of the Joanneum Quarter, the Neue Galerie Graz in the museum building at Neutorgasse 45 was architecturally linked with the historic Joanneum buildings in Raubergasse, which are home to the Natural History Museum and the CoSA - Center of Science Activities.

## Current Exhibitions

[Exhibition\\ \\ Selection   \\ \\ Highlights from the Collection\\ \\ Neue Galerie Graz\\ \\ 29.11.2024 - 31.12.2028](https://www.museum-joanneum.at/en/neue-galerie-graz/our-programme/exhibitions/event/selection-1) [Exhibition\\ \\ Anja Korherr\\ \\ Nightshifters\\ \\ Neue Galerie Graz\\ \\ 19.09.2026 - 31.01.2027](https://www.museum-joanneum.at/en/neue-galerie-graz/our-programme/exhibitions/event/anja-korherr-2) [Exhibition\\ \\ Otto Beckmann\\ \\ Autopoeme\\ \\ Neue Galerie Graz\\ \\ 06.11.2026 - 07.02.2027](https://www.museum-joanneum.at/en/neue-galerie-graz/our-programme/exhibitions/event/otto-beckmann-3) [Exhibition\\ \\ Trauma and Body\\ \\ Hannes Schwarz, Walter Pichler and Bruno Gironcoli\\ \\ Neue Galerie Graz\\ \\ 13.11.2026 - 11.04.2027](https://www.museum-joanneum.at/en/neue-galerie-graz/our-programme/exhibitions/event/trauma-body)

[Opening\\ \\ Maria Legat\\ \\ Missionary Position\\ \\ Neue Galerie Graz, BRUSEUM\\ \\ 26.11.2026](https://www.museum-joanneum.at/en/neue-galerie-graz/our-programme/calendar/event/maria-legat-3)

BRUSEUM

The BRUSEUM represents a separate collection and research focus on the life and work of the world-famous Styrian artist within the Neue Galerie Graz and has a permanent exhibition area in the Neutorgasse museum building.

[More](https://www.museum-joanneum.at/en/neue-galerie-graz/discover/collection/bruseum)

[Current Exhibitions](https://www.museum-joanneum.at/en/neue-galerie-graz/our-programme/exhibitions/event/extract)

Image Credits

#### Limited accessibility at the BRUSEUM

The BRUSEUM currently has limited accessibility.

For the time being, only the first room, which features works by Günter Brus, is open. The presentation from the collection will be expanded step by step. 

This will allow the BRUSEUM to once again focus more strongly on works by Günter Brus and provide a deeper insight into central aspects of his work, his artistic development and his lasting influence on the Austrian and international avant-garde.

## At the Joanneumsviertel you can also visit ...

### Natural History Museum

The Natural History Museum houses fascinating exhibitions by all the natural sciences departments of the Joanneum Universal Museum: Botany, Geology & Palaeonthology, Mineralogy and Zoology.

[Natural History Museum](https://www.museum-joanneum.at/en/natural-history-museum)

### CoSA - Center of Science Activities

“Please touch” rather than “do not touch”: The CoSA – Center of Science Activities is a science centre dedicated primarily to natural sciences and technology, designed for young people of 12 and over.

[CoSA - Center of Science Activities](https://www.museum-joanneum.at/en/cosa-graz)

### Steiermärkische Landesbibliothek (Styrian State Library)

The oldest and largest of the Austrian State Libraries collects, preserves and administers valuable Styrian cultural heritage. It sees itself as a scientific library with a strong focus on the humanities.

[Steiermärkische Landesbibliothek (Styrian State Library)](https://www.landesbibliothek.steiermark.at/)

# Marisol

A major retrospective of Marisol, icon of pop art. Behind her appealing and humorous work lies a sharp message about the role of women, societal norms, and the way we deal with climate.

[Tickets](https://www.boijmans.nl/en/tickets 'Tickets') [More info](https://www.boijmans.nl/en/exhibitions/marisol 'More info')

Depot

### Go Behind the Scenes at the Depot

Ever wondered what a museum keeps out of sight? Bring your group on a guided tour of the Depot and step inside the world’s first publicly accessible art storage facility. You’ll explore the building and see artworks up close in the storage compartments, a view you won’t get anywhere else.

[Tickets](https://www.boijmans.nl/en/tickets 'Tickets') [More info](https://www.boijmans.nl/en/activities/guided-tour 'More info')

Depot

### Restaurant Renilde

On the sixth floor of the Depot of Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen, high above Rotterdam, you will find Renilde. We serve a menu that changes daily, shaped by the best the season has to offer. Exciting flavours, carefully prepared and shaped by the best seasonal produce.

\* The Depot is accessible only with an online ticket

The Depot of Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen is the world’s first publicly accessible art storage facility. The depot is located next to Museum Boijmans Van Beuningen in Museumpark in Rotterdam. Visitors can see the result of over 175 years of collecting. More than 155,000 objects housed together, arranged in fourteen storage compartments with five different climates. Next to the objects, all the activities that go into preserving and managing a collection are on open view in the building.

[Sneak preview Depot in 45 seconds](https://www.boijmans.nl/en/depot#)

[Discover the Depot](https://www.boijmans.nl/en/depot#discover-the-depot) [Walk-in program](https://www.boijmans.nl/en/depot#walk-in-program) [Restaurant Renilde](https://www.boijmans.nl/en/depot#restaurant-renilde) [Rentals](https://www.boijmans.nl/en/depot#rentals)

## Discover the Depot

The Depot is the first art storage facility in the world that offers access to a museum’s complete collection. The Depot has a different dynamic to that of the museum: there are differnt types of exhibitions, you can wander through the building, surrounded by 155,000 artworks, alone or with a guide, and get behind-the-scenes glimpses of - among other things - conservation and restoration.

[Plan your visit](https://www.boijmans.nl/en/depot/plan-your-depot-visit)

## The Depot: a new museum experience

The Depot is the first art storage facility in the world that offers access to a museum’s complete collection. The Depot has a different dynamic to that of the museum: there are differnt types of exhibitions, you can wander through the building, surrounded by 155,000 artworks, alone or with a guide, and get behind-the-scenes glimpses of - among other things - conservation and restoration.

[Plan your visit](https://www.boijmans.nl/en/depot/plan-your-depot-visit)

And make your own collection

[Buy tickets now](https://www.boijmans.nl/en/tickets) [more information](https://www.boijmans.nl/en/depot/about-depot)

## Walk-in program

Every day, we welcome visitors to the Depot's storage and work areas. Would you like to see the collection up close? Join the Walk-in program and choose which compartment you would like to explore. The start times are indicated at the entrance to the compartments. There is room for a maximum of 13 people per visit. The tours are open to all and last approximately 10 minutes. Would you like more information? Ask a Depot employee in the entrance area of the Depot during your visit.

[Plan your visit](https://www.boijmans.nl/en/tickets)

## Restaurant Renilde

The Depot is known to have dazzling exterior and a spectacular interior. Its roof engulfs you in a green oasis, right in the heart of Rotterdam. It offers spectacular panoramic views of the city and is home to restaurant Renilde, led by chef Jim de Jong. There, an exceptional culinary journey awaits you.

[More about Restaurant Renilde](https://www.boijmans.nl/en/restaurant-lunch-dinner)

# KMSKA, a renovated temple for the arts without equal

Victoriano Moreno

Peter Paul Rubens, Jan van Eyck, Hans Memling, Antoon van Dyck and James Ensor. These are just a few of the grandmasters you will encounter at the KMSKA, the Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp. The KMSKA immerses you in a universe filled with beauty. 

Whoever enters this stately temple on the **Museumplein** enters a different universe. This is where beauty reigns, with an added touch of grandeur. You can already feel it on the stately staircases, you can already see it on the monumental façade and you can already notice it in the entrance hall, which is adorned with magnificent mosaics. And that is just the beginning. Once you stroll through the refurbished museum rooms, you are surprised time and again by breathtaking art. The [Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp](https://kmska.be/en) takes you on a journey of discovery through a host of art styles and grandmasters. 

## Old Masters

[Peter Paul Rubens](https://www.visitflanders.com/en/discover-flanders/arts-and-heritage/flemish-masters/peter-paul-rubens 'Peter Paul Rubens') is an excellent example of this. He is known as one of the most important painters in European history. This **father of the Flemish baroque** was **at home in Antwerp** all his life. The city remains as proud as ever of his legacy, which consists of 2,500 compositions and some 10,000 works of art. This enormous oeuvre of paintings, drawings, book illustrations and even tapestries is also celebrated appropriately at KMSKA. The museum has [a substantial collection](https://kmska.be/en/peter-paul-rubens) of his estate.

Such great art belongs in a monumental location. The **Rubens and Van Dyck Halls** in the KMSKA are more than up to the task. In the hall, which is no less than 15 metres high, Rubens’ altarpieces such as [The Adoration of the Magi](https://kmska.be/en/masterpiece/adoration-magi-6) and [The Baptism of Christ](https://kmska.be/en/masterpiece/baptism-christ-1) hang in dialogue with those of other grandmasters like **Jacob Jordaens** and **Anthony van Dyck**. It makes a person feel small and insignificant, coming face to face with all these monumental masterpieces.

©Karin Borghouts

## Modernists

The old masters are outstandingly represented here, but the more youthful greats are illustrated superbly as well. This is demonstrated by the museum in the snow-white Ensor Wing, dedicated to modern art pioneer [James Ensor](https://www.visitflanders.com/en/discover-flanders/arts-and-heritage/flemish-masters/james-ensor 'James Ensor'). Indeed, KMSKA has the [world’s largest Ensor collection](https://kmska.be/en/james-ensor). Spread over two halls you will find, among other things, [The Oyster Eater](https://kmska.be/en/masterpiece/oyster-eater), [Adam and Eve Expelled from Paradise](https://kmska.be/en/masterpiece/adam-and-eve-expelled-paradise) and [The Intrigue](https://kmska.be/en/masterpiece/intrigue). Among these three milestones in his oeuvre you will also see numerous **still lifes, early bourgeois salons and late seascapes**. These are complemented by four cabinets that showcase the other facets of this remarkable body of work.

Discover all this – and much more – in an impressive setting. On the one hand you will find the old masters (from 1880 and earlier) in the grand XL halls with their beautiful parquet in herringbone. On the other, there is the section of modern art (from 1880 onward). You can experience this in a brand-new building: pearly white and equipped with an equally white, shiny floor. It wasn’t so long ago that these opposite environments saw the light of day.

woodmonkey

## A splendid renovation

In 2011, the museum closed its doors for a total restoration and expansion. A large internal depot was built, as was a new vertical structure that considerably increased the volume of the museum. The grandeur of the historic halls was reinstated. The friezes, busts, medallions and other sculptures in the museum were restored to their full glory. A new state-of-the-art climate system was installed. A brand-new museum garden was created. The scenography was completely rethought. In the end, this tour de force took 11 years. But the result is more than worth it.

Karin Borghouts

Today, the Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp is **one of the most important ambassadors in the Flemish arts landscape**. In the halls of the KMSKA you can admire no fewer than 640 works of art, supplemented by temporary exhibitions. So if you come back to Antwerp, make time to admire all this beauty. You won’t regret it.

# Antwerp

©Havenbedrijf Antwerpen - Peter Knoop

Antwerp is the capital of cool and grandeur. This port city has been seducing anyone with a taste for style for centuries. This was already applicable during the time of Baroque innovator Peter Paul Rubens, and it has not lost an iota of its glamour since.

## Antwerp, Stylish to a Fault

Business travellers, artists, fashionistas and diamond merchants; all can still be found here. Antwerp combines the grandeur of yesteryear with an urban vibrancy. Its Grote Markt and cathedral, Scheldt riverbanks and cobbled streets go hand in hand with a thriving nightlife, galleries and art palaces. It is home to the Rubens House, Plantin-Moretus Museum, Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp (KMSKA), the Museum of Contemporary Art Antwerp (M HKA) and much more… The options in Antwerp are endless, as long as they have that gleam.

## Points of interest

## Museum Plantin-Moretus will reopen on Saturday 5 December

[Museum Plantin-Moretus](https://museumplantinmoretus.be/en/museum-plantin-moretus) is temporarily closed for renovations. During this time, work is being done on an updated visitor route, a new exhibition design and a visitor app. These renovations will make the story of the printing house and the Plantin-Moretus family even more accessible to the general public. Museum Plantin-Moretus will reopen on Saturday 5 December.

## 48 hours in Antwerp, a splendid experience

Time speeds by when you’re in Antwerp. There is so much to experience here, from Baroque master Peter Paul Rubens’s artistic legacy, the Railway Cathedral, the port that is this city’s lifeblood, ground-breaking fashion, sparkling diamonds and much, much more. Prepare yourself for 48 hours in Antwerp.

[Read more](https://www.visitflanders.com/en/inspiring-itineraries/48-hours-antwerp-grandiose-experience)

# Belvedere Palace in Vienna 
More than just a grand building

- [Museums](https://www.austria.info/en-gb/locations/belvedere-palace/#museums)
- [Gardens](https://www.austria.info/en-gb/locations/belvedere-palace/#gardens)
- [Restaurants and hotels](https://www.austria.info/en-gb/locations/belvedere-palace/#restaurants-and-hotels)
- [FAQs](https://www.austria.info/en-gb/locations/belvedere-palace/#faqs)

## Introduction

Baroque architecture meets art history: The Belvedere palaces and museums in Vienna captivate enthusiasts of architecture, history, and art alike.

The Belvedere is far more than just a "palace" – it is an ensemble of two architectural masterpieces: the Lower Belvedere, once the legendary Prince Eugene’s summer retreat, and the Upper Belvedere, renowned for its glittering balls and receptions held beyond the city walls of the time.

Austrian military commander Prince Eugene of Savoy commissioned architect Johann Lukas von Hildebrandt to create his summer residence. Completed in 1723, it reflected the prince's political and military power. Over the years, the complex served not only as a summer retreat but also as a venue for lavish official receptions, balls, and gatherings, as well as housing Prince Eugene’s extensive art collection.

After Prince Eugene’s death, Empress Maria Theresa acquired the complex and transformed the Upper Belvedere into a cultural site for the imperial collections – making it one of the world’s first public museums.

### **Between Art and Architecture**

Today, the Belvedere is one of Vienna’s most iconic landmarks, seamlessly blending history with contemporary art. The Upper Belvedere stands proudly at the centre of the garden, offering spectacular views of its façade from both directions.

In addition to the exhibitions hosted by the Belvedere Museums, visitors can marvel at the architectural highlights of the era, including the _Sala Terrena_, the grand staircase, and the _Carlone Hall_. Meanwhile, the Lower Belvedere – once Prince Eugene’s residence – and the Orangery now house exhibitions and treasures such as the Gold Cabinet, the two-storey Marble Hall, and the State Hall.

### **Lush Gardens and Unparalleled Views**

The French-style gardens, with their symmetrical pathways and ornate sculptures, invite visitors to take a leisurely stroll. Along the way, walkers will encounter contemporary art pieces that add a surprising and modern touch to the historical setting.

Read more

Facts about the Belvedere

From the Upper Belvedere, enjoy the panoramic view, known as the Canaletto View, over Vienna's historic city centre, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

## Schloss Belvedere in allen Perspektiven

---

## Belvedere: the museums

**The Belvedere has been a hub of art from the very beginning.** Initially home to Prince Eugene’s collections, it later housed significant portions of the imperial collection. The opening of the Modern Gallery in the Lower Belvedere in 1903 paved the way for today’s collection, which currently includes 18,600 works spanning 900 years of art history.

Highlights include masterpieces from the Middle Ages, Austrian Baroque, and Viennese Biedermeier, alongside works from Vienna’s turn-of-the-century period. The collection is further enriched by pieces from Claude Monet and Vincent van Gogh, focusing on the 20th and 21st centuries. The **Upper Belvedere hosts the most extensive collection of works by Austrian artist Gustav Klimt**, with iconic paintings such as _The Kiss_ and _Judith_ attracting visitors from around the world. Meanwhile, the Lower Belvedere focuses on rotating exhibitions.

**[Belvedere 21](https://www.belvedere.at/en/visit/belvedere-21)**, located just across the street, is a modern extension inaugurated in its current form in 2011. Designed by architect Karl Schwanzer, this contemporary pavilion showcases modern art and serves as a venue for Austrian and international exhibitions, film screenings, and musical performances.

## Prince Eugene's legacy: The Belvedere through the ages

[Families\\ \\ **The Fantastic Palastics**\\ \\ The augmented reality game invites you to explore the Baroque palace gardens. Search for the animals that once lived here and help prepare them for the future!\\ \\ History meets technology](https://www.belvedere.at/en/game)

---

## The gardens of the Belvedere

[**The Alpine Garden**\\ \\ Visitors can stroll through a historic collection of blooming Alpine plants here. Established in 1803, it is the oldest Alpine garden in Europe.\\ \\ Alpine Garden](https://www.belvedere.at/en/discover/gardens/alpine-garden)

[**The Privy Garden**\\ \\ The former private garden of Prince Eugene, located beside the Orangery, features meticulously designed green spaces, offering a tranquil and intimate atmosphere.\\ \\ Privy Garden](https://www.belvedere.at/en/discover/gardens/privy-garden)

[**Botanical Garden**\\ \\ A hidden gem: The Botanical Garden is both a sanctuary of nature conservation and a touch of wilderness – one of Vienna's largest inner-city green spaces.\\ \\ Botanical Garden](https://www.belvedere.at/en/discover/gardens/botanical-garden)

[**Palace Gardens**\\ \\ Inspired by French design, the palace garden stretches symmetrically between the two palaces: enjoy a leisurely stroll and take in the famous Canaletto View over Vienna.\\ \\ Palace Gardens](https://www.belvedere.at/en/discover/gardens/palace-gardens)

[**Sculpture Garden at the Belvedere 21**\\ \\ Free art experiences at Belvedere 21: International works and sculptures blend seamlessly with the architecture – a stage for contemporary creativity.\\ \\ Sculpture Garden](https://www.belvedere.at/en/discover/gardens/sculpture-garden)

[FoodDrinks\\ \\ **Restaurant Stöckl im Park**\\ \\ Enjoy traditional Austrian dishes alongside innovative beers from the in-house brewery, all under the shade of centuries-old trees, right next to the Belvedere.\\ \\ Stöckl im Park](https://www.stoecklimpark.at/en/)

## Social and ecological sustainability

Heritage preservation aims to permanently maintain and utilise historic buildings. By conserving and restoring structures such as castles, palaces, and monuments, resources like building materials are saved, and land sealing caused by new construction is avoided.

This preservation of valuable historic buildings contributes to climate protection, while also safeguarding traditional craftsmanship. Ancient materials and building techniques require ancient knowledge and expertise.

Through accessibility and inclusion in art and cultural experiences, social sustainability is strengthened, fostering respectful coexistence.

mainEntity.name: When was the Belvedere Palace built?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Upper Belvedere was built from 1717 to 1723, and the Lower Belvedere from 1712 to 1716, based on the designs of architect Johann Lucas von Hildebrandt.

Over the course of three centuries, it served as a residence for both Prince Eugene of Savoy and the heir to the throne, Franz Ferdinand. It was the site of splendid events before becoming one of the first public museums in the world.

mainEntity.name: Where can I see the painting "The Kiss"?

acceptedAnswer.text: The famous painting "The Kiss" by Gustav Klimt is housed in the Belvedere Museum, in the Upper Belvedere.

The Canaletto View of Vienna offers a panoramic look at the Inner City, seen from the terrace of the Upper Belvedere. The view is named after the Italian painter Bernardo Bellotto, who painted several depictions of Vienna from this vantage point in the 18th century. The original painting features the Karlskirche, St. Stephen's Cathedral, and the Salesianerinnenkirche.

# Classical Art Museums: Genuine Masterpieces

Potsdam: Der Jahrhundertschritt von Wolfgang Mattheuer vor dem Museum Barberini ©TMB-Fotoarchiv (Steffen Lehmann)

The fact that some of the works in art museums are several centuries old does not mean that they are just dusty cultural artefacts. On the contrary! Most museums display their treasures to their best advantage, be it in refurbished spaces or via digital media devices.

 [Give “germany.travel” priority on Google](https://google.com/preferences/source?q=germany.travel 'Give “germany.travel” priority on Google')

## Old Masters Art Gallery: Superstars of the Renaissance

 **Dresden: The Old Masters Picture Gallery** ©DZT (Francesco Carovillano)

Almost every visitor to Dresden has the Zwinger on their itinerary. No wonder, since the impressive building complex is one of Germany's most important baroque buildings. Not to mention the interior features! The [Old Masters Art Gallery](https://gemaeldegalerie.skd.museum/en/ 'Old Masters Art Gallery') housed here is one of the most renowned collections of paintings in the world. The "Who's Who" of painting, from Peter Paul Rubens to Albrecht Dürer, is gathered across three floors, focusing in particular on the Renaissance period. More than 300 paintings from across the 15th to 18th centuries, including Vermeer's "The Procuress", Correggio's "Nativity", Titian's "Sleeping Venus" and Raphael's "Sistine Madonna" with its two iconic angels, are on display in the gallery's high, light-filled rooms. The collections of pastels by Rosalba Carriera and paintings by Lucas Cranach are also unique. The goal is to linger instead of rushing through. Especially since the museum has really smartened itself up in 2020. In addition to the careful but decisive modernisation of the building, numerous works were restored, and frames freshly gilded or recreated from scratch. Additionally, extensive accent lighting allows paintings and sculptures to appear literally in the best possible light. A special highlight of the newly-designed Semper Gallery is the integration of the renowned so-called Sculpture Collection, with sculptural works spanning five millennia, from Assyrian relief panels to valuable terracottas and vases.

## Städel Museum: 700 Years of Art History Under One Roof

 **Frankfurt/Main: Städel Museum** ©#visitfrankfurt (Holger Ullmann)

Frankfurt is not only a financial centre, but also a museum capital. A phenomenal 38 exhibition venues, from the Film Museum to the Architecture Museum to the Jewish Museum, make up the "Museumsufer Frankfurt", an unparalleled cultural hotspot. Right in the middle: the [Städel Museum](https://www.staedelmuseum.de/en 'Städel Museum'), one of the most important art museums in the country. Founded in 1815 by the banker and merchant Johann Friedrich Städel, the museum collection is the oldest and most renowned in the country. Over the years, it has collected more than 3,100 paintings, 660 sculptures, 5,000 photographs and over 100,000 drawings and graphics. In imposingly designed rooms, paintings from across seven centuries are presented, from the 14th century to the present day. Many of these are true masterpieces of European art. Would you like to hear some name dropping? Here you go: Hieronymus Bosch, Lucas Cranach, Albrecht Dürer and Sandro Botticelli are represented there, as are Francis Bacon, Gerhard Richter and Wolfgang Tillmans. A real crowd-pleaser is "Goethe in the Roman Campagna" by J. H. Wilhelm Tischbein, probably the best-known painting of the Frankfurt-born Prince of Poets. Those who prefer a more modern approach are likely to enjoy the Goethe silkscreen created by Andy Warhol. Speaking of modern: although these works of art are antique, the museum curators rely on modern apps to serve as audio guides, as well as podcasts, a large digital library with details on each painting, and innovative events including art talks, evening events and workshops for all ages.

## Museum Barberini: The New Pilgrimage Site for Lovers of Impressionism

 **Potsdam: Der Jahrhundertschritt von Wolfgang Mattheuer vor dem Museum Barberini** ©TMB-Fotoarchiv (Steffen Lehmann)

Conversions, renovations, expansions: these things happen regularly in museums, but it is rare for a completely new museum to be commissioned. In 2017, this happened anew with the [Barberini Art Museum](https://www.museum-barberini.de/en/ 'Barberini Art Museum') in Potsdam, which 'The Guardian' immediately ranked among the most important openings of the year internationally. Its prominent location in the new historical centre of Potsdam is particularly noteworthy, as the 18th-century Barberini Palace, which was destroyed in the Second World War, was lavishly reconstructed in the classicist-baroque style. Patron and SAP co-founder Hasso Plattner invested heavily in this, and in a total of 17 exhibition halls, all equipped with the latest technology and featuring high ceilings. Exactly how much is not known. It is also difficult to put a figure on the treasures of the Hasso Plattner Foundation on display across 2,200 square metres. Fact: this permanent exhibition is of great value on its own, being shown alongside high-calibre temporary exhibitions. It focuses on works of French Impressionism and Post-Impressionism; there are around three dozen works by Claude Monet alone (highlight: the Haystacks series). Another focus is on GDR art. These include works by Gerhard Richter as well as by the founders of the Leipzig School, such as Werner Tübke, Bernhard Heisig and Wolfgang Mattheuer. A monumental cast of his sculpture "Step of Century" adorns the museum's inner courtyard.

## The Pinakotheks in Munich: Masterpieces Around Every Corner

 **Munich: Pinakothek of Modern Art** ©www.nicanorgarcia.com (Nicanor Garcia)

The Kunstareal in Maxvorstadt is home to a cluster of top-class museums. Internationally best known are the [three Pinakothek museums](https://www.pinakothek.de/en 'three Pinakothek museums'), where visitors can admire great art from the 13th century to the present day. The Alte Pinakothek, which was the largest museum building in the world when it opened in 1836, contains, nominally speaking, the comparatively oldest works. And what a collection it is! For example, Altdorfer's legendary "The Battle of Alexander at Issus", Dürer's famous self-portrait, Leonardo da Vinci's youthful work "Madonna of the Carnation" and "The Great Last Judgement" by Rubens. At over six metres high, it is the largest painting by this brilliant artist. Masterpieces of no lesser importance, but dating from the late 18th to the early 20th century – including works by Klimt, Manet, Goya, Van Gogh – are part of the collection of the Neue Pinakothek (currently under renovation). As if these two renowned museums were not enough, the Pinakothek Modern, opened in 2002, now brings the total to four. Within the bright, classically sleek building is the Modern Art Collection, with numerous paintings from the 20th and 21st centuries (including works by Paul Klee, Franz Marc and Ernst Ludwig Kirchner), the Architecture Museum, the State Collection of Prints and Drawings and the New Collection, which is one of the most important design departments in the world.

## Introduction

Museums and galleries in Austria are tranquil oases where paintings, sculptures, and modern works inspire and uplift the soul.

### A journey through art history

Museums and galleries offer a fantastic way to explore a country’s culture. They share personal stories and reveal both past and present. Austria’s museums and galleries bring a fresh charm, drawing in art lovers from around the world.

From Vienna’s grand Museum of Applied Arts to the contemporary Kunsthaus in Bregenz, there’s a wide range of art to enjoy. Here, history meets modern art, creating inspiring spaces full of creativity. Exhibitions invite you to step into a world of beauty, where each brushstroke and sculpture can leave a lasting impression.

Visiting these cultural gems gives a glimpse into art's journey through time and brings a sense of ease and freedom. Museums and galleries in Austria are lively places for connection and discovery. Embrace the inspiration, gain new perspectives, and enjoy Austria’s artistic treasures.

---

## Austria's most famous museums

[CarinthiaArt\\ \\ **Carinthian Museum of Modern Art**\\ \\ Carinthia's pop art artist Kiki Kogelnik was part of the same group as Roy Lichtenstein and Andy Warhol.\\ \\ Museum of Modern Art](https://www.visitcarinthia.at/attractions/quality-seal/museum-of-modern-art/ )

[Upper AustriaArt\\ \\ **Ars Electronica Center in Linz**\\ \\ The Museum of the Future offers insights into digital computer worlds, technologies, and media.\\ \\ Ars Electronica Center](https://ars.electronica.art/center/en/)

[Upper AustriaArt\\ \\ **Lentos Kunstmuseum in Linz**\\ \\ The 5,100 m² / 1.2 acre LED facade right by the banks of the Danube alone is a reason to visit – and the exhibitions are even more impressive.\\ \\ Lentos Kunstmuseum](https://www.lentos.at/en)

[Lower AustriaHistory\\ \\ **Austrian Masonic Museum at Rosenau Castle in Zwettl**\\ \\ The design of the castle features secret numerical symbolism typical of Freemasonry.\\ \\ Masonic Museum Schloss Rosenau](https://www.freimaurermuseum.at/en/)

[SalzburgerLandArt\\ \\ **Hangar-7 in Salzburg**\\ \\ Impressive architecture, historic aircraft, and spectacular art combined with moments of pure indulgence.\\ \\ Hangar-7](https://www.hangar-7.com/en/)

[SalzburgerLandHistory\\ \\ **Fortress Hohensalzburg in Salzburg**\\ \\ The 900-year-old fortress is the largest fully preserved castle complex in Europe, towering above the old town.\\ \\ Fortress Hohensalzburg](https://www.salzburg-burgen.at/en/hohensalzburg-castle/)

[SalzburgerLandHistory\\ \\ **DomQuartier Salzburg**\\ \\ In 11 halls of the former Prince-Archbishop's residence, the DomQuartier showcases European paintings from the 16th to 19th centuries.\\ \\ DomQuartier](https://www.domquartier.at/en/)

[StyriaArt\\ \\ **Kunsthaus Graz**\\ \\ Futuristic architecture meets contemporary art: a masterpiece of creativity and innovation.\\ \\ Kunsthaus Graz](https://www.museum-joanneum.at/en/kunsthaus-graz)

[StyriaHistory\\ \\ **Eggenberg Palace in Graz**\\ \\ The palace is an architectural allegory of the universe. The complex now houses a museum.\\ \\ Schloss Eggenberg](https://www.museum-joanneum.at/en/palace-and-gardens-schloss-eggenberg)

[TirolArt\\ \\ **Swarovski Kristallwelten in Wattens**\\ \\ For Swarovski's centenary, André Heller created the Crystal Worlds in the form of a giant.\\ \\ Swarovski Kristallwelten](https://kristallwelten.swarovski.com/Content.Node/wattens/index.en.html)

[TirolHistory\\ \\ **Ambras Castle in Innsbruck**\\ \\ The world's first museum still showcases treasures from the 16th century collection of Archduke Ferdinand II.\\ \\ Ambras Castle](https://www.austria.info/en-us/locations/ambras-castle/)

[TirolHistory\\ \\ **Imperial Palace Innsbruck**\\ \\ The "Maximilian I" exhibition honours the knight and emperor from the House of Habsburg.\\ \\ Imperial Palace Innsbruck](https://www.burghauptmannschaft.at/en/Businesses/Imperial-Palace-Innsbruck.html)

[VorarlbergHistory\\ \\ **Vorarlberg Museum in Bregenz**\\ \\ The focus of this award-winning museum is on archaeology, history, and folklore.\\ \\ Vorarlberg Museum](https://www.vorarlbergmuseum.at/en/)

[ViennaArt\\ \\ **Albertina in Vienna**\\ \\ The Albertina is home to one of the world’s most significant graphic art collections, with Albrecht Dürer’s iconic "Young Hare" as its highlight.\\ \\ Albertina](https://www.albertina.at/en/)

[ViennaHistory\\ \\ **Schönbrunn Palace in Vienna**\\ \\ Majestic splendour, nature, and an unforgettable view – visiting the castle is falling in love.\\ \\ Schönbrunn Palace](https://www.austria.info/en-us/locations/schoenbrunn-palace/)

[ViennaArt\\ \\ **MAK in Vienna**\\ \\ The MAK focuses on applied arts, design, architecture, and contemporary art.\\ \\ MAK](https://www.mak.at/en)

[ViennaArt\\ \\ **MQ in Vienna**\\ \\ The former imperial stables in Vienna have been transformed into a vibrant cultural district.\\ \\ MuseumsQuartier](https://www.mqw.at/en/)

[ViennaArt\\ \\ **Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna**\\ \\ The impressive building, with its lavish interior, provides the perfect setting for world-famous paintings.\\ \\ Kunsthistorisches Museum](https://www.khm.at/en/)

[ViennaHistory\\ \\ **Imperial Palace Vienna**\\ \\ The Imperial Palace, or Hofburg, is home to nine museums, offering a unique collection of grand history!\\ \\ Imperial Palace Vienna](https://www.austria.info/en-us/locations/hofburg-palace/)

[ViennaArt\\ \\ **Leopold Museum in Vienna**\\ \\ Here, you can see the world’s largest collection of Egon Schiele works and hundreds of masterpieces from the Vienna Secession.\\ \\ Leopold Museum](https://www.leopoldmuseum.org/en)

[ViennaArt\\ \\ **Heidi Horten Collection in Vienna**\\ \\ The Heidi Horten Collection showcases the diversity and depth of 20th and 21st-century modern art.\\ \\ Heidi Horten Collection](https://hortencollection.com/en)

---

## Austria's most famous art galleries

[Burgenland\\ \\ **Burgenland State Gallery in Eisenstadt**\\ \\ For those who enjoy a fresh perspective, contemporary and modern art take centre stage here, featuring visual art, installations, and media art.\\ \\ Burgenland State Gallery](https://landesgalerie-burgenland.at/)

[Lower Austria\\ \\ **State Gallery of Lower Austria in Krems**\\ \\ From visual art and performance to new media disciplines, the museum’s range is as impressive as its architecture.\\ \\ State Gallery of Lower Austria](https://www.lgnoe.at/en?set_language=en)

[Upper Austria\\ \\ **Mural Harbor Gallery in Linz**\\ \\ In the Danube Harbour, you'll find one of the largest outdoor street art galleries in the world. Over 300 murals and graffiti pieces are on display.\\ \\ Mural Harbor Gallery](https://muralharbor.at/)

[SalzburgerLand\\ \\ **Thaddaeus Ropac in Salzburg**\\ \\ Ropac is one of Austria's most renowned gallery owners. He focuses on contemporary painting and sculpture exhibitions and introduces new names to the art world.\\ \\ Thaddaeus Ropac](https://www.ropac.net/)

[SalzburgerLand\\ \\ **Gallery Nikolaus Ruzicska in Salzburg**\\ \\ Historic walls, modern architecture, and contemporary art: That’s what you’ll find in the gallery, housed in a former carriage workshop.\\ \\ Nikolaus Ruzicska](https://www.ruzicska.com/)

[SalzburgerLand\\ \\ **Rudolf Budja Gallery in Salzburg**\\ \\ The focus of the gallery at Palais Küenburg is on art historical and current transformations, featuring works from Andy Warhol and Roy Lichtenstein to Keith Haring.\\ \\ Rudolf Budja](https://www.salzburg-altstadt.at/en/business-directory/rudolf-budja-galerie_c_8052)

[SalzburgerLand\\ \\ **Salzburg Foundation**\\ \\ Their two-hour "Walk of Modern Art" creates an art parcours that also incorporates sacred elements, such as the Romanesque choir crypt of Salzburg's first cathedral.\\ \\ Walk of Modern Art](https://www.salzburg.info/en/salzburg/creative-salzburg/art-in-public-room/walk-of-modern-art)

[Styria\\ \\ **Neue Galerie Graz**\\ \\ The range spans from 19th-century artists to the present day, covering classical painting, graphic art, photography, and installation art.\\ \\ Neue Galerie Graz](https://www.museum-joanneum.at/en/neue-galerie-graz)

[Vienna\\ \\ **The Belvedere in Vienna**\\ \\ A central stage for art from the Middle Ages to contemporary works, it houses the world’s largest collection of Gustav Klimt’s art, including the iconic piece "The Kiss."\\ \\ Belvedere Vienna](https://www.austria.info/en-us/locations/belvedere-palace/)

## Immerse yourself in art: Museums and galleries are oases of calm and creativity.

[Party. Celebrate. Art.](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qQk-aplWWF8)

---

## Museum parties: Art, music, and culture in Vienna

Pulsating beats, exclusive exhibitions, and an electrifying atmosphere where art and celebration become one.

[MuseumsMusic\\ \\ **Parties at the Museum of Applied Arts in Vienna**\\ \\ (young)MAK: This young collective organises workshops, talks, exhibitions, and parties that bring fresh ideas and perspectives to life.\\ \\ (young)MAK](https://www.mak.at/en/youngMAK)

[MuseumsMusic\\ \\ **Parties at the Kunsthistorisches Museum Vienna**\\ \\ Once a month, the domed hall transforms into a cocktail bar: Acompanied by beats from top DJs, you’ll hear fascinating stories about the artworks.\\ \\ Kunstschatzi](https://www.khm.at/en/explore/offers/kunstschatzi/)

---

## Where art meets culinary delights

Austria shows how art and cuisine blend together: places where contemporary creativity meets fine flavours. Here, moments of pleasure are created that delight both body and mind – surprising, vibrant and full of variety.

[Vienna\\ \\ **Leopold Museum x Café Leopold**\\ \\ A world-class museum presents Austrian modernism – from Schiele to Klimt and Kokoschka – complemented by urban cuisine with an international twist.\\ \\ Leopold Museum x Café Leopold](https://www.leopoldmuseum.org/en/visit/cafe)

[Upper Austria\\ \\ **Lentos x Lentos Restaurant**\\ \\ An iconic building with panoramic views of the Danube combines modern masterpieces and stylish cuisine. A meeting place in Linz that brings art and enjoyment together.\\ \\ Lentos x Lentos Restaurant](https://www.lentos.at/en/besuch/restaurant)

[Vorarlberg\\ \\ **Kunsthaus Bregenz x KUB Café**\\ \\ A building that redefines light and space presents contemporary art. Next door, a café-bar with cosmopolitan flair and seasonal cuisine awaits.\\ \\ Kunsthaus Bregenz x KUB Café Bar](https://www.kunsthaus-bregenz.at/en/visit/kub-cafe-bar)

[Tirol\\ \\ **Haus der Musik x Das Brahms**\\ \\ Where music lives and modern architecture gives Innsbruck a new stage, urban flair and fine Tyrolean cuisine meet cosmopolitan sophistication.\\ \\ Haus der Musik x Brahms Restaurant](https://www.falstaff.com/en/restaurants/das-brahms-kulturgastronomie-im-haus-der-musik-innsbruck-innsbruck)

[Vienna\\ \\ **Wien Museum x Trude & Töchter**\\ \\ A universal museum in the heart of Vienna tells stories about the city – complemented by cuisine that serves up tradition and modernity with a seasonal & regional focus.\\ \\ Wien Museum x Trude & Töchter](https://www.trudeund.at/en/welcome/)

[Vienna\\ \\ **Albertina Modern x Hausbar**\\ \\ Where Vienna's newest museum puts modern art in the spotlight, a culinary gem with creative menus, cocktail artistry and seasonal cuisine is hidden away next door.\\ \\ Albertina Modern x Hausbar](https://guide.michelin.com/at/en/vienna/wien/restaurant/hausbar-wien)

[Styria\\ \\ **Kunsthaus Graz x Kunsthauscafé**\\ \\ A futuristic museum for contemporary art and, at the same time, an urban meeting place with a creative culinary offering, trendy flair and regular events.\\ \\ Kunsthaus Graz x Kunsthauscafé](https://kunsthauscafe.co.at/en)

[Lower Austria\\ \\ **Kunstmeile Krems x Poldi Fitzka**\\ \\ Between the clean lines of an iconic building, a piece of Krems history unfolds – retold on the plate, inspired by a culinary legend.\\ \\ Kunstmeile Krems x Poldi Fitzka](https://www.donau.com/en/the-danube-in-lower-austria/imx/jakobsweg/poldi-fitzka/)

[SalzburgerLand\\ \\ **Hangar 7 x Mayday Bar**\\ \\ A glass hangar in Salzburg filled with exhibits becomes a complete experience: architecture, aviation technology and art merge with cocktails and culinary creations.\\ \\ Hangar 7 x Mayday Bar](https://www.hangar-7.com/en/culinary)

---

## Open-air museums: Glimpse into life from centuries past

An open-air museum offers a window into past lifestyles and regional cultures. Explore historic buildings, discover traditional crafts, and enjoy a blend of history and nature.

**Open Air Museums**

[Burgenland\\ \\ Burgenland\\ \\ **Where Monks once dwelled**](https://www.dorfmuseum.at/)

[**Weinviertler village museum Niedersulz**\\ \\ Lower Austria](https://www.museumsdorf.at/en)

[**Tirol Farmstead museum**\\ \\ Tirol](https://www.tyrol.com/things-to-do/attractions/all-attractions/a-museum-of-tyrolean-farms)

[**Open air museum Großgmain**\\ \\ SalzburgerLand](https://www.freilichtmuseum.com/en/visitors-information.html)

[**Open air museum Stübing**\\ \\ Styria](https://www.freilichtmuseum.com/en/visitors-information.html)

---

## Museums for kids: Exciting discoveries for everyone

From science and technology to art, culture, history, and society, Austria offers a wide range of museums that are perfect for kids. So, let the adventure begin!

[Burgenland\\ \\ **Petronell Carnuntum**\\ \\ Carnuntum is like a time portal to the ancient world, with houses faithfully reconstructed to their original form.\\ \\ Petronell Carnuntum](https://www.carnuntum.at/en)

[Upper Austria\\ \\ **Castle museum Linz**\\ \\ The modern universal museum showcases the history of nature, culture, and technology from the origins of life to the present day.\\ \\ Castle museum Linz](https://www.linztourismus.at/en/leisure/discover-linz/museums-and-exhibitions/castle-museum)

[Tirol\\ \\ **The Golden Roof museum**\\ \\ Explore the history of the Golden Roof through exciting, interactive stations. Fun and learning for the whole family!\\ \\ The Golden Roof museum](https://www.innsbruck.info/en/sightseeing/sightseeing/museums/detail/infrastruktur/the-golden-roof-museum-innsbruck.html)

[Vorarlberg\\ \\ **Inatura Dornbirn**\\ \\ In the museum, interactive games and video projections are just as much a part of the experience as live small animals.\\ \\ Inatura Dornbirn](https://www.inatura.at/en/)

[Vienna\\ \\ **ZOOM childrens museum**\\ \\ Where learning becomes an adventure: Interactive exhibits, creative workshops, and fun for little explorers and budding scientists.\\ \\ ZOOM childrens museum](https://www.mqw.at/en/institutions/zoom-kindermuseum)

[Vienna\\ \\ **Children's museum Schönbrunn**\\ \\ The children’s museum in the palace brings the history of the imperial family to life – including a quadrille dance class for little princes and princesses in costume!\\ \\ Children's museum Schönbrunn](https://www.kindermuseumschoenbrunn.at/en/)

[Vienna\\ \\ **House of Music Vienna**\\ \\ The goal of the Sound Museum is to inspire understanding, openness, and enthusiasm for music in a playful way.\\ \\ House of Music](https://www.hdm.at/en/)

[Vienna\\ \\ **Mozarthaus Vienna**\\ \\ Dive into Mozart’s world, explore his home, and experience the magic of his music in a fun, interactive way.\\ \\ Mozarthaus](https://www.mozarthausvienna.at/en)

[Vienna\\ \\ **Museum of Natural History Vienna**\\ \\ Rocks, volcanoes, dinosaurs, and countless – often extraordinary – animals: what more could a child’s heart desire?\\ \\ Naturhistorisches Museum](https://www.nhm-wien.ac.at/en)

[Vienna\\ \\ **Vienna Museum of Science and Technology**\\ \\ Exciting exhibits and interactive stations bring the history of technology to life. A special highlight is the mine.\\ \\ Technisches Museum](https://www.technischesmuseum.at/en)

[PalaceCastle\\ \\ **Palace and castle tours for kids**\\ \\ Dreamy castles and majestic fortresses offer a magical journey through time, where kids can conquer the world of noble knights and fair maidens.\\ \\ Palace and castle tours](https://www.austria.info/en-us/activities/castle-and-palace-tours-for-children/)

---

Inclusion in museums

## Physical and digital accessibility

Inclusion in museums goes beyond physical accessibility. It means creating experiences that allow people with disabilities to plan and enjoy their visit independently. This includes presenting exhibits and collections in ways that engage multiple senses and offer diverse information formats. Inclusive options for events, tours, and workshops are also key.

For example, the **Lentos Art Museum** in Linz offers sign language tours and provides easy-to-understand texts, both in print and digital formats, explaining the collection. Visitors with visual impairments are welcome to bring guide dogs.

The **Kunsthistorisches Museum** in Vienna offers art viewings designed for visitors with visual or cognitive impairments. They provide tactile tours and special programs for people with dementia and their caregivers.

Climate Protection Info

## Social sustainability

[Historic preservation](https://www.austria.info/en-us/inspiration/sustainable-travel/) is very important for conserving and maintaining historical buildings. By restoring structures like castles and palaces, we save resources, reduce the need for new construction, and prevent land sealing.

This preservation not only supports climate protection but also helps maintain traditional craftsmanship. Ancient materials and construction methods rely on timeless knowledge and skills.

Incorporating [accessibility and inclusion](https://www.austria.info/en-us/planning/accessible-travel/) in art and cultural experiences enhances social sustainability and fosters a considerate, inclusive approach to shared experiences.

mainEntity.name: Where can I see works by Gustav Klimt?

acceptedAnswer.text: Anyone wishing to admire Klimt's works in Austria will also be treated to some of the country's finest architecture. Whether it’s the modern Leopold Museum, the Vienna Secession, or the imperial halls of the Upper Belvedere, each offers a unique setting. A special gem is the Klimt Villa in Vienna-Hietzing, where the painter used the garden house as his studio during his final creative period.The Belvedere holds the largest collection of works by Gustav Klimt, including world-famous paintings like "The Kiss" and "Judith", which attract visitors from around the globe.

# Art & Museums

Luxembourg has over 60 art and history museums, galleries and cultural heritage spaces.

The capital has several leading museums located within a stone’s throw of each other on the “Museumsmile”. Fans of fine, modern and contemporary art can get their fix at museums like Casino Luxembourg, Villa Vauban and the Mudam Museum of Modern Art. Designed by architect Ieoh Ming Pei, who also designed the Louvre in Paris, the Mudam building itself is a work of art that should not be missed.

## Art as a stroll

THE GOOD LIFE: LUXEMBOURG CITY’S MUSEUMSMILE

The compact capital truly makes museum visits a stroll. The so-called “MuseumSmile” is home to seven museums, a mile that forms a smile, and not just when plotted on the map.

[Read story](https://www.visitluxembourg.com/get-to-know-luxembourg/art-as-a-stroll)

Het gebouw, dat werd ontworpen door de Chinees-Amerikaanse architect Ieoh Ming Pei, is op zich al een bezoek waard.** Mudam is een plek voor puur esthetisch genot. Het gebouw, dat werd ontworpen door de Chinees-Amerikaanse architect Ieoh Ming Pei, is op zich al een bezoek waard. Als museum voor hedendaagse kunst brengt Mudam een breed scala aan kunstdisciplines samen, waaronder schilderkunst, beeldhouwkunst, design en performance. Het museum is gebouwd op de historische site van het Fort Thüngen in het Dräi Eechelen Park en integreert de funderingen van het fort in zijn architectuur. Op sommige plaatsen blijven ze zichtbaar, elders gaan ze naadloos over in de parkomgeving. Ook in het park, dat een prachtig uitzicht over de stad biedt, bevinden zich werken uit de vaste collectie en uit tijdelijke tentoonstellingen. Naast de tentoonstellingen heeft Mudam ook een rijk publieksprogramma. Met uw ticket kunt u regelmatig deelnemen aan activiteiten en workshops. Het museum organiseert bovendien het hele jaar door een brede waaier aan evenementen. Het loont dus de moeite om het programma te bekijken voorafgaand aan uw bezoek. Het museum herbergt ook het café-restaurant Chiche!, een project dat sociale cohesie bevordert. U kunt er genieten van een maaltijd of even halthouden voor een kopje koffie voor of na uw bezoek. --- #### Praktische informatie - Shop - Rolstoel toegang --- #### Cultuur info - Shop - Cafetaria - Kunst - Kluisje --- #### LuxembourgPass - Gratis toegang met de LuxembourgPass ## Openingstijden Openingstijden zijn onder voorbehoud. # Ateneum Art Museum

The Ateneum is the home of Finnish art. Our collection spans from the 18th century to Modernism. In total, our collection includes nearly 30,000 national treasures.

Our highly popular exhibitions showcase international and Finnish art. Paired with our topical research, our exhibitions provide new information and perspectives to our visitors.

We also encourage our visitors to engage in the different encounters our museum offers. You can converse, listen to music, create art, investigate and be inspired.

Our museum attracts thousands of children and young people every year. Our rich educational programme brings art to schools to form part of children’s school work.

Together with the Museum of Contemporary Art Kiasma and the Sinebrychoff Art Museum, we form the Finnish National Gallery. The Finnish National Gallery is Finland’s largest art museum institution and its operations are governed by special legislation.

With art, you are never alone. Welcome to Ateneum!

# Amos Rex

Amos Rex is an art museum where the past, present and future meet. Located within the functionalist landmark of Lasipalatsi, the newly built domed exhibition spaces lie under the distinctively undulating Lasipalatsi square. Amos Rex presents site-sensitive, experiential, and often technologically experimental exhibitions by contemporary artists and their Modernist predecessors. Amos Rex is owned by Föreningen Konstsamfundet.

# House of Art Munich

The House of Art in Munich's English Garden is one of the world's leading galleries. Every year, it hosts around eight exhibitions dedicated to contemporary art.

 [Give “germany.travel” priority on Google](https://google.com/preferences/source?q=germany.travel 'Give “germany.travel” priority on Google')

As one of the world's leading galleries, the House of Art hosts fascinating retrospectives on contemporary artists and special themed exhibitions. The gallery has a turbulent past of its own too, having been used as part of the propaganda efforts in Nazi Germany, when Adolf Hitler opened up the "House of German Art" as a museum and place of self-glorification. Traditional, academic art was put on display here, away from the "Degenerate Art" of the modern age.

Works that didn't represent the accepted traditions were confiscated across the country and confined to the infamous "Degenerate Art" exhibition just a stone's throw from the building. This is where no end of artwork by contemporary artists and groups of painters such as the "Bridge" and "Blue Rider" ended up. The House of Art was used by the US occupying forces as an officers' mess after the Second World War, before eventually being transformed into a museum for modern and contemporary art of international renown. Opening times: Monday to Sunday: 10 am–8 pm, Thursday: 10 am – 10 pm

# Kunst­historisches Museum

Our world-famous [collection](https://www.khm.at/en/artworks) shows objects from five millennia.

**Open daily** in October, November and December!

**Open daily** in October, November and December!

[A 2,000-Year-Old Mystery](https://www.khm.at/en/exhibitions/crime-scene-ephesus)

Crime Scene Ephesus 
[Find out more](https://www.khm.at/en/exhibitions/crime-scene-ephesus)

A 2,000-Year-Old Mystery

Embark on your own investigation and discover the mystery surrounding a mysterious tomb and an unsolved murder in ancient Ephesus. 

An exhibition by the Kunsthistorisches Museum at the **Neue Hofburg | Weltmuseum Wien**

Until 29 March 2027

## Highlights

One of the world’s leading museums, our rich holdings comprise objects from five millennia, from Ancient Egypt to the late eighteenth century.

[Explore collections arrow\_outward](https://www.khm.at/en/exhibitions#permanent-exhibitions)

## Old masters

In the ‘Old Masters’ series, we portray key Renaissance and Baroque artists whose works characterise the Kunsthistorisches Museum. Art historians shed light on the life and work of painters such as Arcimboldo, Bruegel and the Bassano family - in-depth, vivid and with surprising insights.

# The Kröller-Müller Museum

The Kröller-Müller museum in Gelderland boasts not only a world-famous collection of 19th and 20th century art, but also an immense collection of pieces by [Vincent van Gogh](https://www.holland.com/global/tourism/experience/current/van-gogh 'Rural Van Gogh'). If you’re an art lover and you’re in Gelderland, you cannot afford to miss this chance.

- Discover the Kröller-Müller museum’s splendid sculpture park.
- Take a walk through the 25-acre sculpture park.
- Discover the unique Van Gogh collection.

## Home museum

Helene Kröller-Müller had a dream to create her own ‘museum-home’. With her wealthy husband’s money and help from an advisor, she purchased over 11,500 art objects. The Kröller-Müller Museum opened its doors in 1938 in the Hoge Veluwe National Park.

## Van Gogh and the Sculpture Garden

There’s plenty to see at the Kröller-Müller Museum, but these are the two particularly interesting highlights:

- **The Van Gogh collection:** the largest privately owned collection of Van Goghs in the world (not counting the collection of the Van Gogh family itself).
- **The sculpture garden:** has grown into one of the largest of Europe. Surrounded by the De Hoge Veluwe National Park, it’s wonderful to see how the sculptures, garden and park merge together. 

## Art in the Park

Combine nature and culture by visiting the Kröller-Müller Museum in [Hoge Veluwe National Park](https://www.holland.com/global/tourism/getting-around/interests/natural-areas/national-park-de-hoge-veluwe-6 'De Hoge Veluwe National Park'). If you take one of [the free-to-use white bikes](https://www.holland.com/media-bewerken-1/free-white-bicycles-veluwe 'Free white bicycles Veluwe'), you can enjoy the surroundings in the morning and visit the Kröller-Müller Museum in the afternoon.

### Frequently Asked Questions

- What is the Kröller-Müller Museum?

 The Kröller-Müller Museum is a modern art museum. It boast the next-to-largest collection of paintings and drawings by Van Gogh. The collection of 19th and 20th century art embraces top works by celebrated artists, including Claude Monet, Pablo Picasso, and Piet Mondrian. The Kröller-Müller Museum also includes an impressive sculpture garden in the large surrounding park.

- Is the Kröller-Müller Museum worth a visit?

 The Kröller-Müller Museum is well worth a visit. The museum boasts the world’s biggest private collection of Van Gogh paintings. It also features an impressive permanent collection of 19th and 20th century art. The museum is surrounded by a beautifully maintained park with one of Europe’s biggest sculpture gardens. In short, it is a real must-see museum for art lovers.

- What attractions and landmarks are near the Kröller-Müller Museum?

 Attractions and landmarks near the Kröller-Müller museum include the adjoining Hoge Veluwe National Park, one of the biggest single nature reserves in the Netherlands. When visiting the park, make sure to check out the beautiful Sint Hubertus hunting lodge, which was built by the wealthy Kröller-Müller couple. Less than half an hour away is the Nederlands Watermuseum in Arnhem, a modern and interactive museum that explains everything there is to know about fresh water. Museum Bronbeek in Arnhem is the place to go if you want to learn all about the military and colonial past of the Dutch in the Dutch East Indies. There are several great animal parks nearby. In Burgers’ Zoo Arnhem, you can see the most exotic animals in their natural habitat. And Apenheul near Apeldoorn showcases special monkey colonies in their natural habitat.

# Museums to visit in the Netherlands

Although there may be a shortage of hills in the Netherlands, there is one thing you will find in abundance here – museums. In fact, there are over [600 museums](https://longreads.cbs.nl/the-netherlands-in-numbers-2022/how-many-museums-are-there/ 'https://longreads.cbs.nl/the-netherlands-in-numbers-2022/how-many-museums-are-there/') to explore. So, if you are planning a trip here, make sure to schedule time to visit a few. They range from famous art galleries and history museums to smaller, local exhibitions outside the major cities. Whether you are travelling alone, with friends or with family, there really is something for everyone.

- See world-famous artworks first-hand.
- Be amazed by Dutch scientific innovations.
- Learn more about the Netherlands’ diverse history.

## Uncover Dutch history

© Ernst Wagensveld via NBTC

Exceptional museums throughout the Netherlands showcase the versatility of Dutch art. The [Groninger Museum](https://www.groningermuseum.nl/en 'https://www.groningermuseum.nl/en') is home to groundbreaking design, while [Museum Arnhem](https://www.museumarnhem.nl/en 'https://www.museumarnhem.nl/en') highlights contemporary themes. The [Singer Laren](https://www.singerlaren.nl/en 'https://www.singerlaren.nl/en') museum and concert hall in Laren links modernism with nature and culture, and [Beelden aan Zee](https://www.beeldenaanzee.nl/en 'https://www.beeldenaanzee.nl/en') in Scheveningen is all about sculptures on the coast. In short, wherever you are in our beautiful country, you will always find museums to pique your interest.

Does the thought of stories steeped in history set your pulse racing? Step back in time at one of the many historical museums in the Netherlands. Uncover how the past has shaped the Netherlands into what it is today – from everyday life to historical eras such as the [Dutch Era](https://www.holland.com/global/tourism/getting-around/interests/dutch-era 'Dutch Era'), and monumental events such as the Second World War.

Experience how life really was for the average Dutch person from the 1800s to the 1900s at the [Dutch Open Air Museum](https://www.openluchtmuseum.nl/ontdek?taal=en 'https://www.openluchtmuseum.nl/ontdek?taal=en'). Take a peek inside reconstructed buildings and talk to locals about daily activities such as cooking and crafts. Similarly, the [Zuiderzee Museum](https://www.zuiderzeemuseum.nl/?lang=en 'https://www.zuiderzeemuseum.nl/?lang=en') in Enkhuizen gives an impression of the past lives of people from that area. You’ll find a complete village with more than 140 buildings.

© Peter Kooijman

Beautiful [Museum van Loon](https://www.museumvanloon.nl/en 'https://www.museumvanloon.nl/en'), a private residence built in 1672, offers a glimpse into the lives of the wealthy in the Golden Age. And the [Our Lord in the Attic](https://opsolder.nl/en 'https://opsolder.nl/en') museum in Amsterdam is a fascinating monument hidden in the attic of a 17th-century canal house: a clandestine church from the time of the Protestant Reformation, when catholic church services were banned.

Dutch history is inextricably intertwined with seafaring and trade, and Amsterdam’s [National Maritime Museum](https://www.hetscheepvaartmuseum.com/ 'https://www.hetscheepvaartmuseum.com/') presents 500 years of Dutch maritime history. Furthermore, a dive into the Netherlands’ past is not complete without learning about the country’s experience of the Second World War, German occupation, persecution of Jews and other groups, and the resistance. Make sure to add the following to your travel agenda: [the Freedom Museum](https://freedommuseum.com/ 'https://freedommuseum.com/') (Groesbeek), the [Dutch Resistance Museum](https://www.verzetsmuseum.org/en/world-war-ii-in-the-netherlands 'https://www.verzetsmuseum.org/en/world-war-ii-in-the-netherlands') (Amsterdam), the [Overloon War Museum](https://www.oorlogsmuseum.nl/en/ 'https://www.oorlogsmuseum.nl/en/') (Overloon) and the [Airborne Museum Hartenstein](https://www.airbornemuseum.nl/en/home 'https://www.airbornemuseum.nl/en/home') (Oosterbeek).

> Museums collect, preserve, research, interpret and present an enormous cultural capital that belongs to all of us.

Dutch Museums Association

## **Experience iconic artworks**

© Iris van den Broek at Depot Boijmans van Beuningen

Dutch art and artists are known the world over. Home to Rembrandt, Vermeer, Van Gogh, Mondrian and many others, the Netherlands is often recognized as a ‘land of painters’. From the [Old Masters](https://www.holland.com/global/tourism/experience/nl-in-7-stories/dutch-masters 'Dutch Masters') of the Dutch Era (also known as the Dutch Golden Age) to modern icons and contemporary art installations, there is so much to see during your time here.

Of course, you can visit famous venues such as the [Rijksmuseum](https://www.rijksmuseum.nl/en 'https://www.rijksmuseum.nl/en'), the [Stedelijk Museum](https://www.stedelijk.nl/en 'https://www.stedelijk.nl/en') and the [Van Gogh Museum](https://www.vangoghmuseum.nl/en 'https://www.vangoghmuseum.nl/en') in Amsterdam, the [Mauritshuis](https://www.mauritshuis.nl/en/ 'https://www.mauritshuis.nl/en/') in The Hague or Rotterdam’s [Boijmans van Beunigen](https://www.boijmans.nl/en 'https://www.boijmans.nl/en'). However, don’t overlook other locations. The Netherlands is home to over [120 art collections](https://longreads.cbs.nl/the-netherlands-in-numbers-2022/how-many-museums-are-there/ 'https://longreads.cbs.nl/the-netherlands-in-numbers-2022/how-many-museums-are-there/'). In Wassenaar, stroll through the sculpture gardens of [Museum Voorlinden](https://www.voorlinden.nl/?lang=en&gclid=CjwKCAjw-IWkBhBTEiwA2exyO8hnW9uA1plkvbCwAGQJw4638iPrmqSmBJrGSqqn8uvargTyNOB_LBoCE7wQAvD_BwE 'https://www.voorlinden.nl/?lang=en&gclid=CjwKCAjw-IWkBhBTEiwA2exyO8hnW9uA1plkvbCwAGQJw4638iPrmqSmBJrGSqqn8uvargTyNOB_LBoCE7wQAvD_BwE') and take in their stunning selection of contemporary art.

Enjoy the wonderful surroundings of the [Kröller-Müller](https://krollermuller.nl/en 'https://krollermuller.nl/en'), which includes a significant Van Gogh collection and a remarkable sculpture garden. In Haarlem, just a stone’s throw from Amsterdam, you can say hello to Haarlem’s own Old Master at the [Frans Hals Museum](https://www.franshalsmuseum.nl/en/ 'https://www.franshalsmuseum.nl/en/'). And for a closer look at the life of Vincent Van Gogh, visit the artist’s hometown of Nuenen in North Brabant at the [Van Gogh Village Museum](https://www.vangoghbrabant.com/en/home/nuenen 'https://www.vangoghbrabant.com/en/home/nuenen').

## See science in a new light

© Ernst Wagensveld via NBTC

From biology and physics to engineering and space exploration, don your thinking cap at a science museum – big names include Amsterdam’s NEMO and Leiden’s Naturalis. Did you know that the Netherlands is a world leader in scientific research? To maintain this, the [Dutch government](https://www.government.nl/topics/science 'https://www.government.nl/topics/science') invests heavily in this sector (over €4.5 billion per year) to maintain this reputation. Discover the long-standing dedication to this field during your trip.

Is the city of Leiden on your list? If so, stop by [Rijksmuseum Boerhaave](https://rijksmuseumboerhaave.nl/english/ 'https://rijksmuseumboerhaave.nl/english/') to learn more about the history of medicine and scientific accomplishments. Or take a trip to the stars at [Space Expo Noordwijk](https://www.space-expo.nl/en 'https://www.space-expo.nl/en'), where you will uncover the secrets of space travel and out-of-this-world scientific innovations. And for an interactive experience for the whole family, stop by [GeoFort](https://www.geofort.nl/en/home-engels/ 'https://www.geofort.nl/en/home-engels/') in Herwijnen. On this fortress island, learn more about our planet through hands-on activities while also delving into some local natural history.

## Explore quirky exhibitions

© Utrecht Marketing

Alongside the art or science museums that you might expect to see, there are also numerous offbeat locations that are worth exploring. If you are interested in experiencing something a little bit different, these hidden gems could make for a memorable day out. Take [The Cat Cabinet](https://www.kattenkabinet.nl/index.php?option=com_content&view=category&layout=blog&id=42&Itemid=1&lang=en 'https://www.kattenkabinet.nl/index.php?option=com_content&view=category&layout=blog&id=42&Itemid=1&lang=en'), for example, located in a stunning canal house in the city center of Amsterdam. It is here you will find a treasure trove of cat-themed paintings, sculptures and more in this personal family collection that also features works by Pablo Picasso and Rembrandt.

If you are more of a foodie, head to the city of Alkmaar to the [Cheese Museum](https://www.kaasmuseum.nl/en/ 'https://www.kaasmuseum.nl/en/'). You might have already guessed it, but here you can learn about the history of Dutch cheese, see how it’s made and even taste some samples – yummy! Or swing by [Museum Speelklok](https://www.museumspeelklok.nl/lang/en/ 'https://www.museumspeelklok.nl/lang/en/') in Utrecht. A great activity for kids, this museum features a huge range of self-playing instruments, from music boxes to street organs. And if that has tickled your fancy, Amsterdam’s Pianola Museum, which is wholly dedicated to the self-playing player piano, might be for you.

## **Three tips to make the most of your trip**

1. Save money by purchasing a Museum Pass. Although this is an annual pass, if you’re staying for a week or longer and are planning to visit multiple museums, it could be worth it. You can purchase your pass at [various locations](https://www.museum.nl/en/see-and-do/museums?mv-Facilities=SellsMuseumCard&mv-PageIndex=0 'https://www.museum.nl/en/see-and-do/museums?mv-Facilities=SellsMuseumCard&mv-PageIndex=0') in the Netherlands.

2. Make the most of the pleasant weather during the spring and summer months by visiting one of many outdoor museums and exhibitions throughout the country. And while you're here, be sure to read our tips on how to get the most out of a visit to the Netherlands during [spring](https://www.holland.com/global/tourism/getting-around/interests/season/spring 'Spring in the Netherlands') or [summer](https://www.holland.com/global/tourism/getting-around/interests/season/summer 'Summer in the Netherlands').

3. Make sure to look up temporary exhibits ahead of time. Although you may have already visited a certain museum, there are very often new, limited-time-only, collections to discover.

### The Porsche Takes a Break

In 2006, as part of his exhibition at Kunsthaus Bregenz, Vorarlberg artist Gottfried Bechtold lined up eleven concrete Porsche sculptures from his ensemble _Elf Elf_ on Karl-Tizian-Platz. Now, due to the upcoming renovation works at the Vorarlberger Landestheater, the concrete Porsche will temporarily leave its usual location. Throughout the construction period, which is expected to continue until summer 2027, access to Kunsthaus Bregenz will remain unaffected.

### New KUB Editions by KOO JEONG A and Cyprien Gaillard

Originally presented in the KUB exhibition _LAND OF OUSSS \[ GRAVITTA \]_, KOO JEONG A’s edition features two photographs of the Alps taken from an airplane and is available as a set. Cyprien Gaillard’s _O (The Empty Hollow)_ combines flute mouthpieces with zero-euro banknotes. Both editions are available now.

[Read more](https://www.kunsthaus-bregenz.at/en/editions)

### In the Shop: Take Home a Memory of Florentina Holzinger’s Performance

Festival cups in a practical 400 ml size and unique bags made from ripstop parachute silk. These collectible tote bags are feather-light while offering exceptional durability.

The limited editions are available exclusively at the KUB ticket desk!

### KOO JEONG A – LAND OF OUSSS \[ GRAVITTA \]

KOO JEONG A’s works create a delicate balance between the visible and the invisible, subtly challenging our perception of space and time. Exhibition views, reproduced using only silver and black, enter into dialogue with poetic text fragments by the Italian author Federico Nicolao. Together, they create a space in which the works presented in Bregenz can fully unfold their impact.

[Read more](https://www.kunsthaus-bregenz.at/en/publications)

### Podcast "Cloud Castle" – Biennale Special!

In the fourth episode—a special edition of the _Cloud Castle_ podcast—the directors of Bündner Kunstmuseum Chur, Kunsthaus Bregenz, Kunstmuseum Liechtenstein, and Kunstmuseum St.Gallen report directly from Venice on Venice, sharing unfiltered first impressions from the opening days of the 61st Biennale di Venezia.

[Read more](http://www.cloudcastle.art)

### The “House” Moves to Switzerland

In late 2025 Kunsthaus Bregenz opened an international call for proposals presenting concepts for the reuse of the “House” from the previous exhibition ███████. The parasitic object was on view at KUB until January 18, 2026, and is to continue to be used as an artist's residence and exhibition space at City SALTS on the outskirts of Basel. A jury and ███████ selected the project out of some fifty submissions.

[Read more](https://www.kunsthaus-bregenz.at/en/news/call-for-proposals-artistic-reuse-of-the-house-on-view-at-the-current-exhibition)

### Kunsthaus Bregenz was awarded the Austrian Ecolabel

Kunsthaus Bregenz reaches another goal in terms of sustainability: The Institution is now officially part of the Austrian Ecolabel.

The Museum der Moderne Salzburg is responsible for a diverse and broad collection of works, totalling around 55.000 pieces that span from the 19th and 20th century all the way to present day and have a focus on graphics and photography from the beginning.

[Collection overview](https://www.museumdermoderne.at/en/collections/overview/)

## Library & Learning Centre

Lese- und Medienlounge, Museum der Moderne Salzburg © Museum der Moderne Salzburg, Foto: wildbild, Doris Wild

The Generali Foundation Learning Centre is a multifunctional research and learning space, that facilitates the engagement with art from the classic modern period up until the present day. It is open to the public and is located at the Rupertinum location in Salzburg's old town.

[Ticket](https://shop.kunstmeile.at/webshop/webticket/shop?page=timeslot 'Ticket')

© Wolfgang Woessner

- [Exhibitions](https://www.kunstmeile.at/en/institutions/kunsthalle#exhibitions)
- [Events](https://www.kunstmeile.at/en/institutions/kunsthalle#events)
- [About the Museum](https://www.kunstmeile.at/en/institutions/kunsthalle#about-the-museum)
- [Stories](https://www.kunstmeile.at/en/institutions/kunsthalle#stories)
- [Getting There](https://www.kunstmeile.at/en/institutions/kunsthalle#gettingthere)

##### Exhibitions

© Phyllida Barlow Estate. Courtesy the Phyllida Barlow Estate and Hauser & Wirth, Foto: Alex Delfanne

### Exhibition renovation

The Kunsthalle is currently closed for exhibition renovation. The new exhibition, “Phyllida Barlow,” opens on November 21, 2026. [To the Opening](https://www.kunstmeile.at/en/program/events/eroffnung/69907 'To the Opening')

[All Exhibitions](https://www.kunstmeile.at/en/institutions/kunsthalle/uebersicht-ausstellungen)

##### Events

- [© KMK, Foto: Agnes Winkler\\ \\ Every 3rd Sunday of the month, 2.00 p.m.\\ \\ **Family guided tour**](https://www.kunstmeile.at/en/productions/familienfuhrung-kunsthalle/4095)
- [© KMK, Foto: Agnes Winkler\\ \\ Every Sunday & National holiday, 2.00 p.m.\\ \\ **Art Info**](https://www.kunstmeile.at/en/art-education/adults/artinfo)
- [© Phyllida Barlow Estate. Courtesy the Phyllida Barlow Estate and Hauser & Wirth, Foto: Ken Adlard\\ \\ Sat, 21.11.2026, 11.00 a.m.\\ \\ **Exhibition Opening**\\ \\ Phyllida Barlow](https://www.kunstmeile.at/en/program/events/eroffnung/69907)

[Alle Veranstaltungen](https://www.kunstmeile.at/en/program/events?room=343)

© KMK, Foto: Agnes Winkler

### Art info

Meet the art education team directly in the exhibition to engage in inspiring dialogs about art and discuss exciting questions about the objects and the artists. The Kunstinfo gives you exclusive insights into the exhibitions. [More Info](https://www.kunstmeile.at/en/art-education/adults/artinfo 'More Info')

[More Events](https://www.kunstmeile.at/en/program/events)

##### About the Museum

### Architecture

 [Columned hall in the Kunsthalle Krems with paintings on the wall](https://noeku.on.damlivery.com/s/b0f0649e3ab6f556ad4a277de1cf518b/noeku/810912/rm:fit/h:3200/w:3200/q:90/rs:originalSizePng/f:webp/g:fp:0.5:0.5)

© Andreas Hofer

The Kunsthalle Krems unites industrial heritage with modern architecture. Formerly a tobacco factory in the nineteenth century, the building was repurposed by Adolf Krischanitz as a contemporary exhibition hall. Permanent works of art by Eva Schlegel and Peter Kogler grace the interior, giving the Kunsthalle Krems a distinctive atmosphere.

[More Info](https://www.kunstmeile.at/en/institutions/kunsthalle/architecture)

#### Program

 [Director of the Kunsthalle Krems Florian Steininger in the exhibition](https://noeku.on.damlivery.com/s/06bc3c0e428d404ddf3bd71105ceda12/noeku/811694/rm:fit/h:3200/w:3200/q:90/rs:originalSizePng/f:webp/g:fp:0.5:0.5)

© KMK, Foto: Walter Skokanitsch

"My program brings international art to life at the Kunsthalle Krems. Working directly with artists, exhibitions are realized that reflect socially relevant issues from a progressive standpoint. Through collaborations with important partner organizations, critical positions in contemporary art are often presented for the first time in German-speaking countries, thereby shedding light on new developments."

\- Florian Steininger, artistic director of the Kunsthalle Krems

[More Info](https://www.kunstmeile.at/en/institutions/kunsthalle/objectives)

#### History

The Kunsthalle Krems arose from a visionary idea: an old tobacco factory outside the metropolis of Vienna was to be transformed into a modern Kunsthalle. As the first exhibition venue on what is known today as the Kunstmeile Krems, the focus eventually shifted to international contemporary art. Important artists have been featured here including Arnulf Rainer, Yoko Ono, Pipilotti Rist, Hans Ob de Beeck, and Helen Frankenthaler.

[More Info](https://www.kunstmeile.at/en/institutions/kunsthalle/history)

##### Stories

© KMK, Foto: eSeL

### Between Angel and Monster

Interview with Julia Belova Julia Belova's works operate at the interface of spirituality and physicality, tradition and rupture. In “Monstrum Sacrum”, Orthodox and Catholic symbolism merge with an unusual choice of materials that emphasises transparency and brilliance. The eponymous monster's role as either threat or protection, foreign or familiar, remains open. In an interview with curator Andreas Hoffer, she discusses these contrasts. [Read the interview](https://www.kunstmeile.at/en/stories/zwischen-engel-und-monster/1354 'Read the interview')

© Nachlass Anna und Bernhard Blume / Bildrecht, Wien 2024

### Recipe by Anna Blume

In their photographs, Anna and Bernhard Blume turn bourgeois life upside down. Domestic order is literally shattered by flying potatoes and broken dishes. In her private life, Anna Blume was known for her cheese and leek soup. "My mother used to make the soup when we had visitors. I hated it as a child," says Hedwig Blume, Anna and Bernhard Blume's daughter. [Read the Story](https://www.kunstmeile.at/en/stories/kase-lauch-suppe-nach-anna-blume/938 'Read the Story')

© KMK, Foto: eSeL

### Interview with Christian Gonzenbach

The Swiss artist Christian Gonzenbach works as a researcher at the interface between natural sciences and artistic approaches. For the Dominican Church the artist designed a temporary installation. Andreas Hoffer, curator of the exhibition, spoke to the artist about his approach to the work in Krems. [Read more](https://www.kunstmeile.at/en/stories/poetry-of-transformation/650 'Read more')

[Plan Your Route](https://www.kunstmeile.at/en/visit/gettingthere/directions-to-the-museums)
