#### About the Museum

##### ARCHITECTURE

The State Gallery of Lower Austria in Krems is a unique architectural jewel situated at the gateway to the Wachau UNESCO World Heritage Site. The building is characterized by its dynamism, innovation, and boldness. These are also the leitmotifs of the exhibition program under artistic director Gerda Ridler.

[read more](https://www.kunstmeile.at/en/institutions/landesgalerie/architecture?v=2511)

##### Program

 [Director Gerda Ridler in front of a work of art showing horses.](https://noeku.on.damlivery.com/s/92e0549bc587eb04475f156d88299420/noeku/810840/rm:fit/h:3200/w:3200/q:90/rs:originalSizePng/f:webp/g:fp:0.5:0.5)

© KMK, Foto: Raffael F. Lehner

Gerda Ridler has been the artistic director of the State Gallery of Lower Austria since 2022. The art historian, cultural manager, and art expert draws on the bold architecture’s distinctive features as the leitmotifs for her program. Oriented around three pillars, the program makes the State Gallery of Lower Austria a dynamic exhibition venue both architecturally and artistically.

The State Gallery of Lower Austria serves first as a stage for showcasing the art treasures of the state of Lower Austria and second as a location for presenting the work of local artists. The third pillar of the program opens a window to international art.

[read more](https://www.kunstmeile.at/en/institutions/landesgalerie/program)

> I associate the striking architecture of the building with dynamism, innovation, and daring. These are also the leitmotifs of my program.”

Gerda Ridler, artistic director

#### Stories

© Claudia Larcher/Bildrecht Wien

### ELEVATOR WITH LINGUISTIC MISTAKE

What does a car sound like when it moves horizontally? And what about an elevator when it moves vertically? The State Gallery of Lower Austria inspires visitors with artistic interventions. [More Info](https://www.kunstmeile.at/de/stories/lift-mit-sprachfehler/770 'More Info')

© KMK

### MY MUSEUM - young people help shape the future

Since 2019, the Landesgalerie Niederösterreich has been inviting young people to actively help shape the museum and contribute their creativity with the "My Museum" project series. [More Info](https://www.kunstmeile.at/de/stories/my-museum-junge-menschen-gestalten-mit/771 'More Info')

### Getting There

[Plan Your Route](https://www.kunstmeile.at/en/institutions/www.kunstmeile.at/en/visit/gettingthere/directions-to-the-museums)

# Home

- Exhibition

### [Scultori Fiamminghi](https://www.mleuven.be/en/programme/scultori-fiamminghi)

In the autumn of 2026, M will, for the first time, highlight the artistic exchange between Italy and the Low Countries in the 16th century. Featuring masterpieces from renowned international museums, the exhibition tells the fascinating story of mutual influence, virtuoso craftsmanship, and a drive for innovation.

[Tell me more](https://www.mleuven.be/en/programme/scultori-fiamminghi 'Tell me more')

09.10

28.02.27

Egidio della Riviera (attributed to), Three Sleeping Putti © Galleria Borghese, photo: Luciano Romano

[Tell me more](https://www.mleuven.be/en/programme/scultori-fiamminghi 'Tell me more')

- Exhibition
- Collection

### [Collection of M](https://www.mleuven.be/en/programme/collection-of-m)

The collection of M’ spans several centuries: from ancient masters to contemporary makers and everything in between. The presentation showcases the richness of this collection and challenges you to actively look. Masterpieces and little-known gems guide you along unexpected parallels and highlight pressing societal questions of our time.

[Tell me more](https://www.mleuven.be/en/programme/collection-of-m 'Tell me more')

29.06.24

29.04.29

‘Marshes of Genk’ (detail), Rodolphe de Lexhy, 1894, Collection M Leuven, CC0, source: artinflanders.be, photo: Cedric Verhelst | ‘I Sea’ (detail), Tina Gillen, 2018, Flemish Community Collection at M Leuven, photo: © the artist

[Tell me more](https://www.mleuven.be/en/programme/collection-of-m 'Tell me more')

- Exhibition

### [Els Nouwen](https://www.mleuven.be/en/programme/els-nouwen)

Els Nouwen’s work is hard to pin down. Her paintings typically begin with a photographic image, either from the media, art history or her personal archive, that she transfers to canvas with great technical precision. However, just when it seems settled, the disruption begins. 

[Tell me more](https://www.mleuven.be/en/programme/els-nouwen 'Tell me more')

30.01

22.11

‘Cauliflower Ears XOOOO’ © Kristel Van Ballaer

[Tell me more](https://www.mleuven.be/en/programme/els-nouwen 'Tell me more')

On location St Peter's Church

- Exhibition
- Collection

### [Experience Bouts](https://www.mleuven.be/en/programme/experience-bouts)

Just around the corner from M, the restored St Peter’s Church is the setting for a new sensory experience. M will guide you through the fascinating story of this Gothic church and help you renew your acquaintance with its art treasures: masterpieces by Flemish Masters in their authentic context.

[Tell me more](https://www.mleuven.be/en/programme/experience-bouts 'Tell me more')

Permanent

Dieric Bouts, 'Het Laatste Avondmaal', Collectie M Leuven, foto: Dominique Provost voor Meemoo, Art in Flanders

[Tell me more](https://www.mleuven.be/en/programme/experience-bouts 'Tell me more')

### [Elise El Yousfi presentation](https://www.mleuven.be/en/elise-el-yousfi-presentation)

Elise El Yousfi's presentation marks the culmination of her five-month residency at M. During her residency, she continued to develop a visual practice situated at the intersection of sculpture and poetry. Raised within a Moroccan and French cultural background, El Yousfi’s work explores questions of diaspora, identity, and the experience of growing up. 

[Tell me more](https://www.mleuven.be/en/elise-el-yousfi-presentation 'Tell me more')

09.10

28.03.27

© Kimberley Dhollander voor M Leuven

[Tell me more](https://www.mleuven.be/en/elise-el-yousfi-presentation 'Tell me more')

- Exhibition

### [Nefeli Papadimouli](https://www.mleuven.be/en/programme/nefeli-papadimouli)

With a background in architecture and visual arts, Nefeli Papadimouli works across media, from participatory actions in public space to sculpture, drawing, costume design, moving image, installation and performance. Inspired by phenomenology, feminism and contemporary political theory, she explores spatial configurations of distance as essential elements in processes of social conflict, negotiation and equilibrium.

[Tell me more](https://www.mleuven.be/en/programme/nefeli-papadimouli 'Tell me more')

# Groeningemuseum

Listen

# Groeningemuseum

Listen

[Listen](https://app-eu.readspeaker.com/cgi-bin/rsent?customerid=11150&lang=en&readid=reader-content&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.museabrugge.be%2Fvisit%2Flocations%2Fgroeningemuseum 'Listen to this page using ReadSpeaker webReader')

Don’t miss this chance to visit the Groeningemuseum one last time, before it closes its doors on 11 January for a four-year-long complete refurbishment. You’ll then be able to discover the heart of the Groeninge Collection at BRUSK.

Six centuries of Belgian visual arts in one location, with work by Flemish primitives such as Jan van Eyck, Hans Memling and Gerard David, neo-classicism by Joseph Odevaere and Joseph Ducq, Flemish expressionism, and 20th century modern art by René Magritte, Roger Raveel, Raoul De Keyser

## Flemish primitives

In Groeninge Museum you will find paintings by Jan van Eyck, Hans Memling, Hugo van der Goes, Gerard David, Hieronymus Bosch, Ambrosius Benson, Lancelot Blondeel, father Pourbus and his sons and their contemporaries. They were masters who came from the Low Countries and often worked in Bruges and completed assignments there in the late 15th and early 16th centuries. Several of those paintings are regarded as milestones in the history of European art.

## A bird’s-eye view of six centuries of visual arts

Apart from work by Pieter Bruegel the Younger and Peter Lely, the museum also possesses lots of historical items and flower pieces and various monumental canvases by Jacob van Oost.

The paintings by the Bruges neo-classicists from the latter decades of the 18th and 19th centuries form an impressive ensemble. Artists such as Joseph-Benoît Suvée, Jean Bernard Duvivier, Joseph Ducq, Joseph Odevaere and François Joseph Kinsoen did their formal training in Bruges and thereafter built up international careers with their works of history pieces and refined portraits.

The 19th and 20th centuries are represented by work from Edmond van Hove, Ferdinand Khnopff, Emile Claus and paintings by the Flemish expressionists, by work from Permeke, De Smet, Van de Woestyne and Brusselmans. Groeningemuseum possesses almost all editions of Marcel Broodthaers’ printed work, six works by Georges Van Tongerloo, paintings by Paul Delvaux and René Magritte, and post-war work by Raoul De Keyser and Roger Raveel.

 Available for free at the ticket desk: 

 - **Search game: Activity booklet The Green Feather (+6 years)**

 The ring-necked parakeet (budgie) of Jan van Eyck takes you on an exciting voyage of discovery through the Groeningemuseum. In the task book, he lands not only near the world-famous paintings by the Flemish Primitives, but also near lesser-known works of modern masters. A series of search, look and do-tasks will help you to learn more about six centuries of painting and sculpture. The parakeet will also give you one of his very own green feathers, which you can use to mark your favourite work of art. Which piece deserves a feather in its cap?

## About S.M.A.K.

[More](https://smak.be/en/about-s.m.a.k)

_S.M.A.K. shows art from its own collection in dialogue with works of contemporary artists from all corners of the world. By means of contemporary art, we seek and give meaning to this complex and fragmented world. In doing so, we make every effort to be accessible and inclusive, because art is for everyone. Meet artists with a surprising and visionary view of the world and sharpen your perspective. Slowly recover from the many impressions at [_Wilde Weide_](https://smak.be/en/smak-cafe) or by taking a walk in the park._
